canonical_name: map_elites (MAP-Elites module for Sferes2) -- Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites (Mouret, J. B., & Clune, J. (2015) per README reference; module authors Jean-Baptiste Mouret and Danesh Tarapore; Inria per author e-mail, copyright headers ISIR / UPMC; 2015-2017)
lineage: README: 'MAP-Elites module for Sferes2', reference 'Mouret, J. B., & Clune, J. (2015). Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites'; every licensed header says 'This file is a part of the sferes2 framework.' and the module builds via use='sferes2' with includes '../../' (i.e. lives at sferes2/modules/map_elites). sferes2's README at its own pin says 'we will soon integrate a more flexible version in the master branch of sferes_v2', i.e. this module is the standalone precursor of the later in-tree QD code. || main loop (reader, from the code): Per generation MapElites::epoch() flattens every occupied cell of the boost::multi_array archive into the working population, then Params::pop::size times picks two uniformly random elites, crosses and mutates them into two children, evaluates the whole child batch (in parallel via sferes::eval), and for each child computes its cell from round(desc_i * shape_i) and overwrites the occupant if the cell is empty, the child is fitter by more than epsilon, or it ties and lies closer to the cell centre; sferes2's Ea::run() drives this for nb_gen generations and dumps stats every dump_period.

entry_points: map_elites.hpp sferes::ea::MapElites (SFERES_EA(MapElites, Ea)): random_pop() creates Params::pop::init_size random individuals, evaluates them, adds each to the archive; epoch() gathers all filled cells into _pop, draws Params::pop::size uniform-random parent pairs, cross()+mutate()+develop(), evaluates the batch, _add_to_archive each child

map_elites.hpp MapElites::_add_to_archive(i1, parent): maps fit().desc() to a boost::multi_array<phen_ptr, behav_dim> cell by round(desc*shape), replaces the occupant if empty, better by > Params::ea::epsilon, or tied and closer to cell centre (_dist_center)
map_elites.hpp MapElites::_selection(pop): uniform random pick from the archive contents
fit_map.hpp sferes::fit::FitMap and macro FIT_MAP(Name): fitness base holding a std::vector<float> _desc of size Params::ea::behav_dim in [0,1], set via set_desc()

stat_map.hpp sferes::stat::Map::refresh(ea): every dump_period writes res_dir/archive_<gen>.dat lines 'offset  desc_0 desc_1 ...  fitness  genotype...'; stat_map_binary.hpp MapBinary and binary_map.hpp write/load a binary archive; stat_progress.hpp MapProgress

test_map_elites.cpp BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(map_elites): Rastrigin on EvoFloat<10> in [-5,5], desc = first two genes, behav_shape 128x128, init_size 1000, batch 1000, nb_gen 1001; BOOST_CHECK(best > -1e-3)
extract_binary_map.cpp main(argv[1]): loads a binary_map file and prints dims then 'pos... fit phen...' per elem
plot_map.py <archive.dat> <size>: loads 'k, x, y, z' columns, builds size x size heatmap, saves heatmap.pdf

example.input: No data input; test_map_elites.cpp compiles in the Rastrigin problem and a Params struct (behav_dim 2, epsilon 0, behav_shape 128 128, init_size 1000, size 1000, nb_gen 1001, dump_period 100, parameters min -5 max 5, cross_rate 0.25, mutation_rate 0.1, eta_m 10, eta_c 10, polynomial mutation, sbx crossover)
